description: Scout connector telemetry, session-token accounting, the restrict_tools MCP gate and the two privacy gates. Activate only inside scout runs: SCOUT_MODE from the runner, or, for a session started inside a vault without a runner, the run mode its prompt names (scout/hooks/run_context.py). Interactive sessions are skipped by those. The PreToolUse restrict_tools gate is different: it applies to every session (run or interactive) in a vault whose connectors.custom.yaml uses restrict_tools, the vault being SCOUT_DATA_DIR, else the one containing the working directory; it starts Python only when that file might set the key: the literal text, any backslash (a double-quoted YAML key can spell it with escapes, #590) or a NUL byte, and Python then decides on the parsed file. Elsewhere it exits before starting Python. The privacy gates (#453) count a session as a scheduled run by #517's rule (SCOUT_MODE set, or SCOUT_READER set to anything but exactly owner). kb-read-gate denies a run's shell/Grep/Glob read of knowledge-base/ and action-items/context/ in favour of scoutctl kb (Read stays allowed; an agent:* reader is denied it, and a delegate:<id> reader (#550) is denied a Read of any vault file scoutctl kb wouldn't show it, KB or not, so the Read hook sends every delegate Read to Python); It also denies a run's Bash call that sets, unsets or blanks SCOUT_MODE or SCOUT_READER or clears the environment (env -i), or that detaches (nohup, setsid, disown, a trailing &, launchctl, osascript, open, tmux, screen, script, at, batch, ssh) (#595); the commit hook knows a run's commits from the process table whatever their environment says. It also denies, names and records (event kb_read_gate.hook_skip) a run's git call that skips or redirects the commit hooks: --no-verify or -n where it means that, -c or --config-env or git config on core.hooksPath, alias.* or include.path, GIT_CONFIG_* variables, commit-tree, update-ref on a branch, and a Bash write into .git/hooks or .git/config (#607). It exits in the shell for every other session, and for a run's Bash call that names no KB path, and whose command value has no run-env, detach or hook-skip word, no `scoutctl kb` call feeding xargs, a loop, read or a command substitution, no recursive read (rg, find, tree, du, grep -r or --recursive, ls -R, git grep), and no KB path once its quotes and backslashes are removed, for grep to find. Since the 2026-11 KB audit it also denies a read through a variable or loop holding a KB path, one xargs feeds with KB paths, an input redirection from a KB path, a quoted program (sh -c, eval) that reads the KB, and a recursive read rooted at the vault or above. kb-write-gate (its own hook name, so an engine that predates it fails closed: exit 2) denies a run's Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit into what decides which hooks run (Phase 1b of spec 2026-11-13; scout/kb/hook_paths.py): the vault's git dir (all of it, a worktree's real git dir too), the user's git config (~/.gitconfig, ~/.config/git, $GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL), the agent's settings.json/settings.local.json in the vault's .claude, ~/.claude and $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, its plugin store, and the hook config dirs of other agent CLIs (.codex, .gemini, .agents, .grok, .cursor), after resolving ~, .. and symlinks and ignoring case; a run's Bash write to those agent and git-config paths is denied the same way. Every run write goes to Python (about 40 ms), since a symlink can hide the path from the shell; owner sessions exit in the shell. Both record kb_read_gate.hook_skip. Round 3 of #637: a run's shell write to a path the gate can't work out (a command substitution, a backtick, or a variable set elsewhere) is denied; an inline program (an interpreter's -c or -e program, or a here-document fed to one) is judged only when it writes files or starts programs, by the paths and protected names its own text spells; a shell that runs its stdin (sh <<EOF, | bash) is judged on those commands. Scout's secrets (~/.scout-secrets, $SCOUT_SECRETS_DIR) and the vault's delegate state (.scout-state/delegate-mirrors.json, .scout-state/delegate-scan/, .scout-state/delegate-inbox/) are write-protected, the agents' inbox copies (.scout-inbox/agents/) are read- and write-protected; a run's Read, Grep or Glob of the secrets is denied (the Read hook starts Python in a run when the payload names scout-secrets or $SCOUT_SECRETS_DIR), and a Bash read is denied when the command spells a secret's path (best effort), except the Telegram bot token and chat id. kb-read-label (PostToolUse on Read) attaches the note's privacy label (private: never to a shared surface) in any vault session; it exits in the shell unless the payload names a KB path, and labels a note it can't classify as private. shared-read-record (PostToolUse on Agnes's three shared-notes tools) records what the answer showed in .scout-cache/shared-reads/, so check-outbound recognises it, and tells the session the rule for it; a session in no vault that isn't a run exits in the shell. front-page-reads (PostToolUse on a run's Write, Edit or MultiEdit) warns, never blocks, when the file is a project's front page (<projects_dir>/<name>/<name>.md) and the session's transcript (and its subagents') shows no read of a note under that project's knowledge/ folder; it names only notes the run's reader may see, marks private ones, exits in the shell for owner sessions and for a payload whose file_path isn't shaped <dir>/<x>/<x>.md, starts Python only then, and always exits 0. outbound-gate runs check-outbound on an MCP write tool's input in a vault (Slack as surface slack, others as connector_write): a run is denied, the owner is warned; a session in no vault that isn't a run exits in the shell. Both fail closed for runs (exit 2 when scoutctl can't run). Per #72, per-tool-call accounting was moved out of PostToolUse (which fired one Python cold-start per tool call) into the session-tool-log Stop hook that walks the transcript once at session end.
